match.reason: Neither bank point teaches hypothesis-test errors: the chemistry card covers random and systematic measurement error, and the mathematics card covers absolute error and limits of accuracy in measurement, so no existing point matches the Type I and Type II error idea.

draft.title: Type I and type II errors
card: A test ends in one of two decisions: reject the null hypothesis or do not reject it. Either decision can be wrong, because a sample can mislead.
rejecting a null hypothesis that is true. The test claims an effect that is not really there.
failing to reject a null hypothesis that is false. The test misses an effect that is really there.

Example: H₀ says a new battery lasts the same time as the old one. If the batteries are really the same but the test says they differ, that is a type I error. If the new battery really lasts longer but the test finds no difference, that is a type II error.
draft.remember: Type I: reject a true H₀. Type II: keep a false H₀.

a.q: Which situation describes a type II error?
opts: Not rejecting H₀ when H₀ is false
Rejecting H₀ when H₀ is true
Not rejecting H₀ when H₀ is true
Rejecting H₀ when H₀ is false
a.why: A type II error is a failure to reject a null hypothesis that is actually false, so a real effect is missed. Rejecting a true H₀ is the tempting option, but that is a type I error.
a.clue: Type II means the test missed something real.

b.q: Mia tests H₀: a bakery's loaves have mean mass 700 g. The loaves really do have a mean mass below 700 g, but her sample leads her not to reject H₀. What has happened?
opts: A type II error, because H₀ is false and was kept
A type I error, because H₀ is false and was kept
A type II error, because H₀ is true and was kept
A type I error, because H₀ is true and was rejected
b.why: The true mean is below 700 g, so H₀ is false. Mia did not reject it, which is a type II error. A type I error needs a true H₀ to be rejected, and that did not happen here.
b.clue: First decide whether H₀ is true, then whether Mia rejected it.

a.best: Not rejecting H₀ when H₀ is false

b.best: A type II error, because H₀ is false and was kept

problems.detail: The remember line says 'keep a false H₀', while the card says 'failing to reject'. 'Keep' can suggest accepting or proving H₀, which VCE teaching avoids. 'Fail to reject a false H₀' would match the card. The options in question b also use 'kept'.
